verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā parittaṁ nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsuṁ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha, picking up a little bit of dirt on his fingernail, addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ—yo vāyaṁ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito, ayaṁ vā mahāpathavī”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the little bit of dirt on my fingernail, or this great earth?”

verses.pali: “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṁ, yadidaṁ—mahāpathavī; appamattakāyaṁ bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito.
verses.english: “Sir, the great earth is certainly more. The little bit of dirt on your fingernail is tiny.

verses.pali: Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṁ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the great earth, it doesn’t count, there’s no comparison, it’s not worth a fraction.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, appamattakā te sattā ye majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye paccantimesu janapadesu paccājāyanti aviññātāresu milakkhesu …pe….
verses.english: “In the same way, the sentient beings reborn in central countries are few, while those reborn in the borderlands, among uneducated foreigners, are many. …”
